svg.font-family: IBM Plex Mono, Menlo, Consolas, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace
svg.aria-label: Sequence diagram of one rollout across driver, agent, resources, model server, and inference engine, with plain-language serialization annotations on every hop.

g.text: driver
agent
resources
model server
engine

svg.text: 1 · POST /run — the task row
driver serializes the row to JSON bytes
agent parses JSON, validates into typed models
2 · POST /seed_session — the ENTIRE task payload
agent re-serializes everything it just validated
resources parses it all, then mostly discards it
small acknowledgment (may carry an MCP session token)
3 · POST /v1/responses to ITSELF — a real loopback socket
full serialize → parse → validate round trip in the same process
(open PR #1439 replaces this with a direct function call)
repeated once per model call — the request re-sends the whole conversation each time
4 · POST /v1/responses — prompt + all prior turns
agent deep-copies the request, dumps models to dicts, serializes
model server parses and validates the whole conversation again
5 · engine request
dialect conversion: two more dumps,
two more validations, re-serialize
6 · generation + token IDs + logprobs
model server parses, then validates a list
entry per token — the expensive part
rebuild as a Responses object: 2 dumps + 1 construct-validate
capture (if on) makes its own full copy, hashes, fsyncs
envelope branch (opt-in): token arrays become compact strings here
7 · the response, ~2 MB at training sizes
serialization now orjson (#2867, landed) — see §3 for its alias bug
agent parses AND re-validates the full response, every call
8 · POST /verify — prompt AND final response together
agent: dump → merge → validate → dump AGAIN → serialize
resources: parse + validate the largest payload in the system
verify() computes a reward, then builds its reply by
echoing the whole request back (one more dump + validate)
9 · reward + the full echo — the verifier decides the record

text.tspan: reply bytes now orjson (parity serving branch)

svg.text: agent parses + validates the echo
10 · /run reply = the echo
driver parses, attaches indices,
capture + trajectory data;
this is the training record
driver finalize — on the same event loop that drives all the sockets

g.text: · re-reads and parses the model-call capture file (when observability is on)
· with token capture on: attributes the terminal model call by response id
and content fingerprint, in a pool thread
· serializes the record, writes and flushes it on this loop (fsync only
when token capture retires the rollout)
· keeps every row and result in memory until the run ends
reading the annotations
serialize = Python objects → JSON bytes (orjson)
parse = JSON bytes → Python dicts/lists
validate = dicts → typed Pydantic models,
checking every field (and every list element)
dump = typed models → plain dicts (a full copy)
green = changed by landed or pushed work
why the re-validation everywhere: each server treats every peer as untrusted —
a deliberate isolation choice that costs one full validation per hop per direction.
why the echo: the verifier owns the final record —
whatever the resources server replies is what the driver persists and the trainer consumes.
why cookies ride every arrow: per-rollout state on the resources server —
seed_session, tool calls, and verify are correlated by a signed session cookie the agent forwards.
why history re-sends per model call: the Responses API is stateless per request —
step N's request embeds all N−1 prior turns, so request size grows linearly and total work quadratically.
everything is fully buffered: no hop streams —
each side holds the complete body in memory (bytes + parsed dicts + validated models simultaneously).
